newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO dig in on settlement building.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO dig in on settlement building.

text.p: Israel and the PLO on Wednesday dug in to their opposing positions on Israeli settlement in Jerusalem hours before the sides were to meet under U.S. auspices to try to break a deadlock in peace talks.

Senior PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat said after talks with U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross in self-ruled Jericho the Palestinian side intended to discuss settlements and peace deals at the meeting with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
"We will discuss all issues with Mordechai, specifically settlement activities. If it is not discussed then we will be moving in a vicious circle," Erekat told reporters.

Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said Israel wanted the meeting to restore full cooperation between the sides. But he said Israel's position on the Har Homa settlement, now under construction in Arab East Jerusalem, would not change.
"We will clarify the issues together...It is our responsibility in order to try to return to full cooperation so the process will return to its course," he told Israel Radio.
"Israel's position on Har Homa is known," Levy said.

Negotiations have been largely stalled since Israel broke ground for the settlement on March 18, igniting a wave of Palestinian protest and one Islamic militant bombing in which three Israeli women were killed.
Ross, on his second peace mission in one month, arranged a meeting between Israeli and Palestinian officials at the home of U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk later on Wednesday.
A U.S. official said both sides can raise any issue during the meeting which will begin at 7 p.m. (1600 GMT).

The Palestinians have said they would not agree to resume peace talks until the Jewish state stopped all settlement building, including in East Jerusalem which they envisage as the capital of a future state.
Levy, who is due to meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Washington on Friday, said he hoped for a quick resumption of Israel-PLO negotiations on the implementation of peace accords.
Asked when he wanted to renew the talks, Levy said: "I wish today, yesterday. But we must not give up and we must put things back on a constructive track."

Israel's Haaretz newspaper said last week that Clinton was not interested in a head-on collision with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on the issue of a settlement freeze, fearing a confrontation with the U.S. Congress and with the U.S. Jewish community.
The daily said this was despite the fact that Clinton and Albright were dissatisfied with Netanyahu's continuing Jewish settlement building, which they viewed as harming peace moves.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa urged the United States to take a more active role in reviving Middle East peace talks.

"I urge Amercian diplomacy, which is dynamic, to be more active and to play the role of the honest broker who works to implement the principle of land for peace," Moussa told the London-based Arabic-language daily newspaper al-Hayat.
Netanyahu said on Sunday he was proud of his March decision that sent bulldozers to carve out the Har Homa settlement.
Ross has visited Jordan and Egypt as well as Israel and Palestinian self-rule enclaves during his current mission.

PLO officials have criticised Washington for what they said is its refusal to press Israel to halt settlement activities in Palestinian areas during mediation to restart the talks. Israel says it will not stop settlements.

About 200 supporters of the Islamic Salvation Party, an off-shoot of the Islamic militant Hamas group, marched in self-ruled Gaza on Wednesday against renewing security cooperation between Israel and the Palestinian Authority.
